question.worked_solution:
We start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & -6 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & -6 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -\frac{5}{2} & 5 & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 0 & -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{5}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & -6 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & -6 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to basis vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the reduced matrix has $2$ pivot columns (or alternatively, it has exactly $2$ non-zero rows). 

Therefore, 
$\text{dim}(\text{Span}\{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\})=2.$
